flotilla.copyFiles.description: Glob patterns (relative to the main worktree) of ignored files to copy into new worktrees, e.g. ".env".

flotilla.setupCommand.description: Command to run in a terminal in a new worktree, e.g. "npm install". With flotilla.linkFolders, use a command that keeps what's there (npm install, not npm ci, which deletes node_modules first).

flotilla.linkFolders.markdownDescription: Folders (relative to the main worktree) that a new worktree gets as hard links to the main worktree's, before `#flotilla.setupCommand#` runs, e.g. `["node_modules"]`. Linked files take no extra space, and the setup command installs only what the worktree's branch changes. A hard-linked file is the same file in both worktrees: package managers replace files rather than edit them, so the files that installs and tools do write in place are copied instead (in `node_modules`: `.package-lock.json`, `.bin`, caches such as `.vite`, and packages with install scripts, such as esbuild's). A worktree can then be installed again on another platform (a devcontainer) without touching the main worktree's files. Folders on another drive are skipped.

enumDescriptions: Remove a done ticket's worktree when nothing in it can be lost and nobody is using it; ask otherwise.
Ask before removing any done ticket's worktree.
Never remove worktrees on your behalf.
flotilla.removeFinishedWorktrees.description: What happens to a ticket's worktree once the ticket is Done. Its branch is always kept.

flotilla.autoAdopt.description: Automatically make worktrees inside the repository portable across host and container.

flotilla.defaultBase.description: Base branch for progress and comparisons. Empty: origin/HEAD, then main, then master.

flotilla.activeWindowMinutes.description: A workstream with changes newer than this is 'active'.

flotilla.staleAfterDays.description: A workstream with no activity for this long is 'stale'.

flotilla.agentStatusStaleMinutes.description: A 'working' agent report older than this is shown as last reported.

enumDescriptions: One notification for what needs you (tickets asking a question, ready for review, approved, stopped; worktrees waiting for input or reporting an error), gathered for about a minute. Only the leading window shows it.
A notification for each of those as it happens.
No notifications. The Needs you count in the status bar still shows.
flotilla.notify.description: Which notifications Flotilla shows for what needs you.

enumDescriptions: Notify when a run on a worktree's branch fails.
Notify when a run on a worktree's branch finishes, passed or failed.
Don't notify about CI runs.
flotilla.ci.notify.description: Notify when a CI run you watched (on a worktree's branch) finishes. Only the window that leads the backlog notifies.

flotilla.pollSeconds.description: How often to refresh the worktrees in use (a window open, an agent running, recent changes) while the Workstreams view is visible. Other worktrees are refreshed every few minutes, so a commit on the base branch reaches them within that time; a commit, stage or checkout in a worktree shows there within this interval.

flotilla.tagChatTitles.description: Show the worktree in Claude Code's own session list: chats linked to a worktree are renamed to "<branch>: <title>" once Claude Code has titled them. A title you set yourself is never replaced.

flotilla.search.maxResults.description: Search results per worktree before Flotilla asks you to refine the search or show more.

flotilla.changes.limit.description: Changes shown per worktree (staged and unstaged together) before Flotilla says "and N more". Stage All, Discard All and commits still cover every change; open a terminal in the worktree to see them all.

flotilla.tabLabelPattern.markdownDescription: Regular expression that finds the id to show on a worktree tab (its first group, or the whole match), e.g. `T\d+`. Empty: a Jira key such as `ABC-123`, or an issue number at the start of a branch part (`123-fix` → `#123`); otherwise the last part of the branch.

flotilla.backlog.idPrefix.patternErrorMessage: 2–10 capital letters or digits, starting with a letter, like BL or WEB.
flotilla.backlog.idPrefix.markdownDescription: Prefix of new local backlog item ids, as in `BL-12`, until another one is chosen when adding an item (the backlog then keeps that one). Tabs label worktrees by these ids.

flotilla.backlog.branchPattern.markdownDescription: Branch name for work started from a backlog item. `{id}` is the item's id (e.g. `BL-12`), `{slug}` its title in lower case with dashes.

enumDescriptions: Agents' commits (Claude Code's) in a worktree working on an item must start with its id, like "BL-12: ".
Everyone's commits in such a worktree must start with the item's id.
Commit messages aren't checked.
flotilla.backlog.commitPrefix.markdownDescription: Whose commits in a worktree working on a backlog item must start with the item's id (`BL-12: …`). A git `commit-msg` hook checks it; an existing hook keeps running after it.

flotilla.review.automatic.markdownDescription: When a backlog item goes to In Review (moved there, or its agent reports `Ready for review.`), start a reviewer agent: a different agent that reviews the work and gives a verdict in the ticket. Changes requested go back to the implementer, and the reviewer looks again, until it approves or `#flotilla.review.maxRounds#` is reached. The agents run without a window (`claude -p`); their chats open from the ticket.

flotilla.review.maxRounds.markdownDescription: How many review rounds the reviewer and the implementer go through before the loop stops and leaves the decision to you.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code decides what's safe to do without asking (auto mode).
File edits are allowed; commands only if your Claude Code settings allow them.
Only what your Claude Code settings allow; everything else is refused.
Everything is allowed. Only in a sandbox (a dev container you can throw away).
flotilla.agents.permissionMode.markdownDescription: What agents Flotilla runs without a window (the autopilot's, reviewers, and implementers making the changes asked for) may do. Nobody is there to approve a request, so what isn't allowed is refused. Set in your user settings only: a repository can't change it.

flotilla.agents.model.markdownDescription: The model agents Flotilla starts on tickets use, unless a ticket chooses its own: an alias (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) or a model's full name. Empty: Claude Code's default.

flotilla.agents.lightModel.markdownDescription: The model for tickets marked Light (small, mechanical work: chosen in the ticket, or by the agent that proposed it), e.g. `sonnet`. Their reviewers use `#flotilla.agents.model#`, and a Light ticket moves up to it when its review requests changes a second time or its agent says it needs a stronger model. Empty: no ticket is Light.

flotilla.agents.autoCompactWindow.markdownDescription: The context size, in tokens, that agents Flotilla starts compact against (Claude Code's `autoCompactWindow`, 100000 or more): they summarize their context sooner, so each turn re-reads less. 0: Claude Code's own (the model's whole context window).

flotilla.agents.subagentModel.markdownDescription: The model of the subagents Flotilla's agents start (they search and report back; the agent judges what they find). Never a stronger one than the agent's own. Empty: the agent's own model.

flotilla.agents.guardOutput.markdownDescription: Keep large outputs out of Flotilla's agents' context: a whole read of a file over 400 lines, a plain `cat` of one, or a whole `git diff`/`git show` over 600 changed lines is refused with how to look instead (grep, a line range, `--stat`), and how to get it whole anyway.

flotilla.agents.tokenBudget.markdownDescription: Millions of tokens an agent Flotilla runs may re-read from its context before it's stopped and its ticket asks you whether it goes on (the biggest tickets so far took about 12). An agent that runs the same failing command 4 times in a row with no edit in between is stopped too. 0: no budget.

flotilla.chats.bigContext.markdownDescription: Past this context, in tokens, a chat is marked in the sidebar, and once per chat of yours Flotilla says what it costs: every turn re-reads the whole chat. 0: never.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code's default (your /effort setting).
flotilla.agents.effort.markdownDescription: How hard agents Flotilla starts on tickets think (Claude Code's `--effort`), unless a ticket chooses its own.

flotilla.agents.lean.markdownDescription: Start agents lean: without your skills, plugins and MCP servers, with the coding tools only (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, subagents, the web). Everything an agent starts with is context it re-reads on every turn; this makes it about a quarter smaller. Your own Claude Code sessions keep everything. Agents opened in Claude Code's panel (no model or effort chosen) start as usual.

flotilla.agents.maxRunning.markdownDescription: How many agents Flotilla runs at once, in all: the autopilot's tickets, reviews, revisions after a review, and agents going on after a usage limit. Starts Flotilla makes on its own wait in a queue when it's reached: your replies (answers, requested changes) first, then reviews and revisions, then resumes, then new tickets. Starts you make with a ticket's Start or Start Review run at once, and count toward it. Prioritize starts a queued one now, above the limit (see `#flotilla.agents.maxPrioritized#`).

flotilla.agents.maxPrioritized.markdownDescription: How many agents Prioritize may run above `#flotilla.agents.maxRunning#` at once: a queued start (a reply, a review, new work) that you prioritize starts now. At this ceiling, Prioritize asks which running agent to pause to make room; it goes back to the head of the queue. Prioritize starts nothing while free memory is short (`#flotilla.agents.minFreeMemoryMB#`). 0: Prioritize takes a free slot, and asks for a pause whenever there's none.

flotilla.agents.minFreeMemoryMB.markdownDescription: Free memory (MB) the machine needs before Flotilla starts an agent: each agent's Claude Code process takes about 300 MB, and builds and tests more. The autopilot and reviews wait until there's room; a manual start says so and offers to start anyway. 0 turns the check off.

flotilla.review.model.markdownDescription: The model reviewer agents use. Empty: the ticket's choice, else `#flotilla.agents.model#`.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code's default (your /effort setting).
flotilla.review.effort.markdownDescription: How hard reviewer agents think. Empty: the ticket's choice, else `#flotilla.agents.effort#`.

flotilla.autopilot.avoidClashes.markdownDescription: The autopilot holds back a ticket that would change files a ticket in progress changes (the paths its description names, and those its parent and the tickets it depends on changed), until that one is merged: its work then builds on it instead of being redone after a conflict. A ticket you start yourself always starts.

flotilla.autopilot.maxAgents.markdownDescription: The older name of `#flotilla.agents.maxRunning#`: when set, it's the limit on agents running at once. Empty: `#flotilla.agents.maxRunning#` applies.

flotilla.agents.claudePath.markdownDescription: The Claude Code CLI to run agents with. Empty: the one the Claude Code extension comes with, else `claude` on the PATH. Set in your user settings only: a repository can't change it.

enumDescriptions: Tickets agents add are proposals: they wait in the backlog's Proposed group for you to accept or dismiss them.
Tickets agents add join the backlog at once.
flotilla.backlog.agentTickets.markdownDescription: What happens to tickets agents add to the backlog (any agent can, through `.flotilla/backlog/inbox/`; `.flotilla/backlog/AGENTS.md` tells them how).

flotilla.dev.githubApi.markdownDescription: For development only: the address of the fake GitHub (`npm run fake-github`, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4010`) that the CI/CD view reads instead of GitHub. Read only in the Extension Development Host, and only for a loopback address; a sign-in isn't asked for then.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Flotilla runs git, your setup command and Claude Code hooks in the repository, so it needs a trusted workspace.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Flotilla needs git and the files on disk.
